import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_paths = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_20/test_0.csv"
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
# Use index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per Hint 24
dfs = [pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0) for path in source_paths]

# Since there is only one source table, operate on it directly
df = dfs[0]

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['sex', 'smoker', 'total_bill', 'tip', 'size']
# Group by 'sex' and 'smoker' (categorical columns, leftmost in target schema)
# Aggregate numerical columns 'total_bill', 'tip', 'size' by their average (mean)
# This matches the target examples and previous successful attempts

result = (
    df.groupby(['sex', 'smoker'], as_index=False)
    .agg({
        'total_bill': 'mean',
        'tip': 'mean',
        'size': 'mean'
    })
)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[['sex', 'smoker', 'total_bill', 'tip', 'size']]

# Convert columns to target types explicitly
result['sex'] = result['sex'].astype(str)
result['smoker'] = result['smoker'].astype(str)
result['total_bill'] = result['total_bill'].astype(float)
result['tip'] = result['tip'].astype(float)
result['size'] = result['size'].astype(float)

# Write the transformed data to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_20/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
